mission: Six people in a ship built for two. Sera reaches for controls that do not exist. Torin's warmth fills small spaces. Sera tests Ben with a tactical question about the Corridor route; his intelligence-operative answer earns the first grudging respect.
why_now: First transit chapter after the lock-in. The crew has to make itself into a crew before the Corridor teaches them what they cost one another.
conflict: Sera measures Ben against a standard he cannot yet name — the commander she followed and lost. Torin mediates with easy warmth that makes the small space feel like a team room. Kael says almost nothing, and it costs the air.
turning_point: Sera tests Ben with a tactical question about the route. His answer is pragmatic rather than doctrinal — the kind of reading she did not expect from a modern Jedi. Her posture shifts half a degree.
opening_hook: Ben wedges himself between a supply crate and the bulkhead to check the nav chart — six people in a ship built for two, and the social fabric creaking as loud as the hull
closing_hook: Torin finds Ben alone in the corridor and says something warm about Luke — 'Your father's name carries weight even in our time.' The compliment feels genuine. It also feels like an assessment.
emotional_trajectory: Tension and territorial friction -> unexpected competence demonstration -> uneasy truce

stakes.personal: Ben's leadership credibility with people who fought wars before he was born
stakes.interpersonal: The group's ability to function — fracture here means failure everywhere
stakes.external: Every moment of internal friction is time Veraine is using to get further ahead

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns in hyperspace — cramped common area, corridor, cockpit
sensory_details: The ship straining with extra passengers; Sera's hand closing on blank hull plating where a console used to be; Torin's ease in small spaces and the old-soldier instinct of standing where he will not block a door; Kael folded into a corner, watching
action_beats: Sera reaches for a cockpit control that doesn't exist on a modern ship — her hand closing on blank hull plating
Ben pulls up the Corridor nav chart and traces the route while answering Sera's tactical question
Torin clasps Ben's shoulder in the corridor — a commander's measured grip of acknowledgment
promises_planted: Mere tactical cooperation won't work; the climax demands genuine unity (PP23)
notes: Survivor-displacement texture is the free worldbuilding of this chapter — Sera's reach into empty hull, Torin's adaptive courtesy that is slightly too easy, Kael's silence. Honour the lived-galaxy-texture obligation by letting the modern galaxy feel unfamiliar to three of the characters. Voice: Allston-channel humor in the cramped common area, tightening when Kael's presence changes the room. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, narrate the synthesis-leadership concept. He answers Sera's question, he registers Torin's approval-and-assessment, he notices Kael without approaching him. The phrase 'leading as coordinator of an unstable coalition' is the chapter's structural description, not a line Ben thinks in. Desh in this scene: lie_reinforced in his own arc — professionally competent, emotionally still at arm's length from the larger crisis.
